items.title: Full Of It
items.summary: I get a lot of strange emails. You ever get those?…
items.content_html:
I get a lot of strange emails.

You ever get those?

Strange emails?

Only from you.

I don't mean the scammy type.

Or maybe I do.

I don't know.

Because I never respond.

Rarely click.

But some I do.

I admit it.

I'll open it.

I won't click a link, though.

So don't even try it.

But I'll look at what's sent.

Once in a blue moon.

To add one to the read column.

Unless they put "Re: Blah blah" as the subject.

Never read those.

There's probably a better way to handle emails than to ignore them.

But what can I say?

I've only got so much bandwidth here.

That's a word I used to hear a lot. 

Bandwidth.

When I lived past what I thought I might not, I made a decision.

Now I'm not saying it's a great decision, but here it is:

I'd rather have strangers hate vehemently dislike me, if it meant my family loved me.

Now, sure, I suppose strangers and my family could love me, but that seems like an awful amount of work.

Truly awful.

And that hasn't been what I've seen out in the world.

To be and get both.

Hasn't been what I've seen.

So I made a choice.

My inboxes (sweet mother there's a lot of 'em) are all full.

But so is my belly.

And my heart.

Burp.

Oooh, got one coming out the other end, too.

I best leave it here.

💨

items.title: Spider 2 Y Banana
items.summary: It's NFL preseason. Which means it's the season before the season.
items.content_html:
It's NFL preseason.

Which means it's the season before the season.

The pre.

I used to think this part didn't matter.

But I was wrong.

This is where everything happens.

Now, I couldn't tell you the first thing about football talent evaluation but I will pretend I do.

Like everything.

And NFL preseason is a grand time to do so.

But when you're watching the game, your eyes tend to focus on the ball.

Who's got it.

Where's it going.

All ball.

All the time.

But there's a lot you miss when you focus on the ball.

You miss the blocks.

Or lack thereof.

The routes that got everyone thinking it's a pass.

Selling it.

Guys on the other side all doing their job.

And still getting beat.

All the focus is on the ball.

But all the action is off it.

I suppose there's a lesson there somewhere.

Like when I learned Supreme Court justices never write their published opinions.

It's all the clerks. 

The public's glory goes to the running back who goes to the house.

Not the linemen who set it up.

Although they get their praise from the team and the back later.

What I'm saying is a lot of the true work comes with little fanfare.

Someone should do a psychological study on what makes the best lineman.

What makes the best best nose tackle.

Not physically.

But their mind.

All guts, no glory.

Getting ahead of myself.

Like always.

🏈

"And Ricard goes in for the championship winning touchdown!"

items.title: Full Faith
items.summary: You ever notice, in our favorite stories, how there's a person…
items.content_html:
You ever notice, in our favorite stories, how there's a person who's kinda clueless?

Young person.

Bumbling through life.

That's who most of us want to be, or at least who we relate to the most.

But there's an old(ish) person, too.

One who's got it all figured out.

Been there, done that.

Who can show the young one the way, if the young one would only listen.

And that's sort of the whole point of the story.

Sure, beat the evil dude at the end, fall in love, live happily ever after, but the story is mostly about the oldie teaching the youngun.

The strange part is most of us grow up wanting to be the bumbler.

The Lukes.

The Daniel-sans.

The Rockys.

The Chris Farleys.

🥋

No one wants to be Yoda.

Miyagi.

Mick.

Sensei.

We want to train to fight in the main event.

We don't want to remember being in the main event.

And that's the part that's sort of funny.

Because as I get older, and do things like wonder what my call sign would be if I had a call sign.

Al "Yoda" Chung.

Badarse.

Now I'm pretty(.) tall for my race. I'm golden, not green. Ears stick out but not that much.

But the rest of it works; I like it.

I know I couldn't use it commercially.

But I don't use things commercially.

Just for my own amusement.

I don't know where I'm going with this other than to say:

[In Yoda voice:] Luminous beings are we, not this crude matter.

🤢

Oh, I know where I'm going.

The best stories might be about the bumbler.

The one you root for.

To get it all figured out.

But who you should want to be, what we are all striving for, is the one who already did it.

Who already fought (and hopefully, but not required, won) the good fight.

Who has finished the course.

Who has kept the faith.

And who keeps it to this day.

To legends.

I see you.

Yoda out.

items.title: Clemens and Cheals
items.summary: There's an old line by Mark Twain. He doesn't have any…
items.content_html:
There's an old line by Mark Twain.

He doesn't have any new lines.

But the line I like is the one about troubles.

"I am an old man and have known a great many troubles, but most of them never happened."

Today, I'd like to bonk you on the head.

That's right.

Bonk.

BONK!

You paying attention?

Ok.

How many times do you worry about something that does or doesn't (thankfully) happen?

And how real does that worry feel?

It could and often does take a really good moment or memory and turns it into a negative one.

Or at least, tarnished.

All because of the mind.

Because of your lens.

Many folks who reach a pinnacle, like say a gold medal or world championship or eating a really nice cut of beef, they don't feel elation.

You know what they feel?

Relief.

Oh, thank God.

Ain't that something?

Sure, there's a lot of folks just happy to be there.

But the champions, the fighters, they can finally exhale.

Lay down their swords and shields.

I can rest now.

For a bit.

We all know or will know troubles.

May they be real.

Or not real.

But they will all feel the same.

At the time.

And looking back.

Hopefully, on every single one of them, you will be able to look back (or down) and exhale.

To hits, near-misses, and the other things.

Thank God.

Thank you, God.

"May all your troubles be small ones, son."

items.title: Count Them If You Got Them
items.summary: Count 'em. Right now. Huh? How much you got? Count. I…
items.content_html:
Count 'em.

Right now.

Huh?

How much you got?

Count.

I don't got cash.

I don't mean your wallet.

I mean your blessings.

Count them.

Right now.

I hope you got a high number.

But not too high to make you think that's how the world works.

Or maybe I do.

Maybe I do.

I hope it's not low.

Not too low.

Your count has to be above zero blessings.

Zero blessings is broken.

And I'm sorry if you're broken.

You can glue yourself back together, though.

With molten gold.

It's called Kintsugi.

More beautiful, stronger, than ever.

And to those counting high, well, good for you.

Now appreciate 'em.

When I was the type to get my vehicle detailed (a misspent youth), the big fella that did it would always get a nice extra.

And he'd say, genuinely:

"Thank you for the blessing!"

Which I always thought was a wonderful thing to say.

So for Big T.

And big G.

Thank you for the blessings.

items.title: Call Me Bugs
items.summary: Musings columns are a funny thing. They used to call them…
items.content_html:
Musings columns are a funny thing.

They used to call them blogs but that's just a terrible name.

Blogs.

Yuck.

Not my favorite word.

I tend to write in a way that sometimes contains more meaning than it appears at first glance.

I seek to reward (or at the very least, a muse) the reader for picking up what I'm putting down.

Easter eggs.

Hidden layers.

Buried treasures.

And who doesn't like a treasure hunt?

Not to say all these musings have gems in them.

Some are just turds.

It's part of the fun.

Sifting through all the dirt.

To find the glimmer.

There's a line about glimmer and gold but I don't think it's useful here.

Call me a fool.

🥕

items.title: Over Them Mountains
items.summary: There was a time I could hit a ball a country…
items.content_html:
There was a time I could hit a ball a country mile.

It didn't happen until I was in my 30s.

So that sucks.

But I could.

I could hit a ball into the other fields.

Onto windshields.

Literally rip the hide off 'em.

Now I know I'm starting to sound like Rico Dynamite.

Flinging 🥩s.

My hero.

But what can I say?

I hit bombs.

I haven't picked up a bat in years.

Threw away the one I made in eighth grade not too many years ago.

Still not sure why I did that.

But it was time to put that part of me to rest.

Goodnight.

The thing I learned about hitting (far too late) is you swing down on the ball.

To create lift.

You don't uppercut.

Even though it looks like it.

You generate a back spin on the ball that just crushes it.

Yards it.

Down goes up.

Way up.

Armed with that bit of knowledge, I could still hit 'em out.

But not like I used to.

I'm ok with that.

I'd probably break my coccyx.

⛰

items.title: Infinity / Infinity
items.summary: Cool day today. As far as days go. 8/8. 8.8. I…
items.content_html:
Cool day today.

As far as days go.

8/8.

8.8.

I almost forgot to write.

I suppose I did.

But there's still time.

Thank you for the time.

I don't have much to say.

Except this:

When you sign up for something, do you feel compelled to use all of it to its maximization?

Like you buy a subscription.

And it comes with all sorts of things.

But you only really want the one thing.

Maybe two.

But you feel like by not trying everything, you're somehow "losing" value?

Leaving something on the table.

Perhaps it's just me.

Even if I think the one thing I seek is worth the total price, I still feel like maybe I should try the other stuff since it's basically "free."

And if I don't like the additional stuff, I tend to dislike the subscription in total.

Not worth it.

Yeah, this is pretty much what you get when I almost forget to muse.

I could go on forever forever.

♾♾

items.title: APB
items.summary: For an old(ish) curmudgeon, I'm a happy fellow. Yeah right. No,…
items.content_html:
For an old(ish) curmudgeon, I'm a happy fellow.

Yeah right.

No, I am.

Truly.

Just chipper.

Like if I was in an old movie, I'd be walking with my elbows out, swinging around and circling street lamps.

Helping old ladies across the street.

Tipping my cap to them as I left.

Beaming.

What a kind young oldish man.

Of course, I don't do that.

At least, not anymore.

Ever.

If I did that today, people probably would call a 3-digit number.

I mean, they probably already had the first 2 pre-typed when they saw me.

Elbows out.

Strutting.

Twirling around poles.

Singing.

In the sun.

I don't do rain.

You ain't gonna melt!!!

Yodeling in the golden circle.

...

Be on the lookout for a old(ish) man having a little too much fun. Appears to be singing old show tunes and targeting the elderly.

...

items.title: I Come In Peace
items.summary: As you make your way through this. Through what? Life. Oh.
items.content_html:
As you make your way through this.

Through what?

Life.

Oh.

You attach yourself to certain things.

Like sports teams.

Cliques.

Apparel brands.

Donkeys or elephants.

Flags.

Interests.

Hobbies.

Avocations.

Vocations.

Why?

Most of us do it because it aligns with, or at least represents, a part of us.

It becomes a part of who we are.

There's also some of us who do it because they think it's cool.

Or makes them noticeable.

This is usually folks who, by themselves, would not necessarily be so.

He's talking about luxury watch lovers.

Go Timex!!!

⌚

Nice.

Here's the thing, though.

I'm learning something.

About time.

About time.

I'm learning that this is all meant to divide us.

To keep us busy fighting.

Go Giants!!!

See?

Pay no attention to the man behind the curtain.

As I go up, hopefully I go up, I see that it's all a bit crazy.

I see the world.

And it looks small.

Hello greenish, blue ball.

🌎

With pockets of fights amongst all the pockets of lights.

Everywhere.

Me?

I'm above it all.

Scanning past the pale blue dot.

Looking for aliens.

🛸

Up here.

Starfaring.

💫

Seeing if they wanna rumble.

👽

Or, as Jon B. and Pac used to say, if they're still down.

What you crying for?
